recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what you differentiate with respect to, and what the xy term needs.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate every term with respect to x
steps.margin_note: First mark. Every y that is differentiated leaves a dy/dx behind it. Write the product rule on 3axy out in full before simplifying anything.
steps.memory_tip: Count the y terms you differentiate, then count the dy/dx terms you have written. The two counts must match.
lines: y is not given in terms of x on its own, so differentiate implicitly: every term with respect to x, treating y as a function of x.
The term 3axy is a product of x and y, so it needs the product rule.

recall.must_convey: That every term is differentiated with respect to x, that d/dx(y³) = 3y²(dy/dx), and that 3axy needs the product rule.
accept: differentiate each term with respect to x and treat y as a function of x
the x y term needs the product rule
d by d x of y cubed is three y squared d y by d x
prati term ni x tho differentiate cheyyali, x y ki product rule
implicit differentiation with a d y by d x on every y

steps.why: The equation is a cubic in y, so writing y in terms of x is not useful here. Implicit differentiation is the only practical route, and the product rule on 3axy is the part of it this question tests.
common_mistakes: Writing d/dx(3axy) as 3ay, which drops the x · dy/dx half of the product rule.
Writing d/dx(y³) as 3y² and forgetting the dy/dx factor.

steps.label: Collect the dy/dx terms and solve
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Divide by 3 first, then move the two dy/dx terms to one side and everything else to the other. State y² ≠ ax, where the tangent is vertical.
steps.memory_tip: The numerator and the denominator have the same shape with x and y exchanged: ay − x² over y² − ax.
lines: Divide throughout by 3:  x² + y²(dy/dx) − ay − ax(dy/dx) = 0
Take the dy/dx terms to one side:  (y² − ax)(dy/dx) = ay − x²

recall.must_convey: That the two dy/dx terms are collected on one side, giving dy/dx = (ay − x²)/(y² − ax).
accept: collect the d y by d x terms on one side and divide
d y by d x is a y minus x squared over y squared minus a x
take y squared minus a x common from the d y by d x terms
d y by d x terms ni oka side ki teesukoni divide cheyyali
the answer still has y in it, which is normal for an implicit curve

steps.why: dy/dx appears in two separate terms, so the answer only comes out after those two are taken together. The answer carries both x and y, which is normal for a curve given implicitly.
common_mistakes: Leaving dy/dx on both sides and calling that the answer.
A sign slip when moving 3x² and 3ay across the equals sign.

insider_note: The 3axy term needs the product rule on xy. Divide through by 3 early to keep the numbers small, then collect the dy/dx terms on one side.
